cost_basis: dollars (CodeRouterBench csv cost_usd for a, b; signal call priced at list prices, PRICES); tokens and seconds for the k < a condition

population.rule: tasks on which all 8 released scores are 0 are excluded in EVERY source (the addendum's bcb rule applied uniformly): the smoke report shows the sandbox passes 36-65 % of the recorded responses on such tasks in bcb / ds1000 / lcb (released-harness failures) and the mbpp dim1 zeros are a hidden-function-name artefact no pre-execution signal can predict; dim9 mbpp is entirely all-zero. A sensitivity with the all-zero tasks kept is reported for s and the bound (offline).

sample.second_signal_sample: qwen3-max on a nested subsample of 200 + 200 tasks stratified by source (the relay's qwen3-max latency, bimodal 1.5 s / 62 s, mean 33 s at the 4-worker cap, made the full sample infeasible inside the 2 h script limit)

api.ledger_note: ledger_units_this_run is the delta of the SHARED ledger (other experiments append concurrently); the experiment's own spend is ledger_units_tag_X12b

signal_diagnostics.hex_language_note: the released HumanEval-X scores give partial credit 0.8 on most non-python tasks, so at theta=1 the non-python languages are 'insufficient' and a prompt router that recognises the language predicts H; at theta=0.5 they are sufficient

C2_llm_vs_routers.x12a_note: X12-a values are on the full id_test (2,919 tasks, all 21 cells incl. non-exec sources); the rows above recompute the same released routers on X12-b's 600 sampled id_test tasks

C3_decision_usefulness_vs_ece.note: variants per (state, primary) on the full 600/600 sample: llm_p, llm_label, llm_lines, tfidf_lr, tfidf_lr_uni + 10 released routers x 2 Z-definitions (binary, cross-fitted); the qwen3-max family lives on the 200/200 subsample and is excluded here; semi-synthetic variants excluded; small states (n < 20) excluded

counterfactual_price_ratio.note: SEMI-SYNTHETIC: cost_B rescaled per state so that a/b equals r (probing means); posteriors unchanged; realized on id_test with the rescaled reference cost

hypothesis_violations.lcb_data_gap: 28 lcb recorded responses are empty although the released score is 1 (infra Addendum 2); truth here is the released score, so these tasks are kept

constant_k.note: k varies with prompt length; the state mean enters net VOI

hypothesis_violations.truth_caveats: lcb (private tests; sandbox agreement 0.73-0.92) and ds1000 (0.65) rely on the released score as truth; hex non-python and dim9 scores are partial-credit / proxy scores (theta=1 treats <1 as insufficient)
hypothesis_violations.signal_model_thinking: deepseek-v4-pro with thinking disabled (cost); the forecast is a single forward pass

claims.statement: No realized gross VOI of any usage of the LLM signal (or of any other signal valued here) exceeds the perfect-information bound min{s(b-a), a(1-s)} from probing; net VOI <= bound - k
claims.kind: IDENTITY-like inequality on expectations, realized OUT-OF-SAMPLE (probing primitives, id_test outcomes; LIVE signal)
claims.verdict: PASS (qualified: point violations without CI support)

claims.statement: Valued state by state (7 sources, theta=1, both primaries, task-weighted), the LLM signal captures more of the perfect-information value than a TF-IDF logistic router trained on the same 600 probing prompts, and is not below the released routers valued on the same id_test tasks
claims.kind: OUT-OF-SAMPLE (LIVE signal; paired task bootstrap on the same resamples, aggregated over disjoint source states)
claims.verdict_rule: task-weighted paired aggregate over the 7 source states (theta=1, both primaries): PASS if the CI of gross_bw(llm_p) - gross_bw(tfidf_lr) is above 0 and llm_p is not CI-below the best released router; FAIL if the TF-IDF difference is CI-below 0; else INCONCLUSIVE

claims.statement: Within (state, primary), the Blackwell capture ratio follows decision usefulness (AUROC; switch share) more than calibration (ECE) across signal variants
claims.verdict_rule: group bootstrap CI of mean(|rho(capture_bw, AUROC)| - |rho(capture_bw, ECE)|) over (state, primary) groups with >= 5 real variants: PASS if above 0, FAIL if below 0

claims.statement: Re-thresholding recovers the value a miscalibrated score loses under the native rule 'attempt iff s_hat >= a/b': the Blackwell usage (calibrated posterior at a/b) is invariant to the monotone shrinkage p/10, beats the native rule on the shrunk score (paired, task-weighted over source states), and is never CI-below the native rule on the real LLM score
claims.verdict_rule: source states, theta=1, both primaries: (i) max |capture_bw(real) - capture_bw(p/10)| < 1e-6; (ii) task-weighted paired CI of gross_bw - gross_native_ab for the shrunk score above 0; (iii) the real score's Blackwell usage is CI-below its native a/b usage in no state

claims.statement: cor:info-vs-proposer: buy routing information rather than upgrade the primary (Qwen3-Max / kimi-k2.5 -> a costlier recorded primary) iff b*Delta p < a(1-s); sign agreement on decided rows; also the actual-signal version [k + C_BW] vs the upgraded cascade
The LLM signal is affordable, k < a, in every state for the primaries it forecasts (Qwen3-Max, kimi-k2.5); for cheaper primaries (qwen3.5-plus) it may cost more than the attempt
claims.kind: LIVE measurement (signal tokens x list price; tokens; seconds) against probing a
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff k_peak < a in every non-small state for Qwen3-Max and kimi-k2.5; qwen3.5-plus reported

pooled_gross_bw_llm_p_qwen_theta1.note: isotonic regression re-implemented in pure Python (unique-x averaging, weighted PAVA, linear interpolation with clipping, as sklearn)
